A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 15-page versions of the same ALLD research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MOS prediction, A/B comparison and synthetic-word detection experiments in Tables 1–4, with ablations and additional experiments in Figure 3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main evaluations, ablations and Appendix A experiments.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation procedure and ALLD method remain identical, including warm-up finetuning, response sampling, the expert reference LLM and the distillation objective in Section 4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same NISQA MOS and A/B tasks, unseen-domain evaluations, LibriSpeech synthetic-word detection task, and auxiliary speech/audio tasks in Appendix A.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including CNN-SA-AP, WavLM, Wav2vec2, SALMONN, Qwen-Audio and Qwen2-Audio tuning variants. The full-finetuning comparison, random SWD baseline and Appendix C model set are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and the appendices retain the same data splits, sample counts, model configurations, training settings and evaluation procedures. This includes the 30k/3k SWD training/test sizes and the LCC, SRCC, MSE, BLEU and accuracy metrics.

E4.justification: The training-data ablation in Figure 3, unseen-domain tests, joint-training comparisons, description-removal experiment and manual-description case study are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same in-context-learning failure analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both retain the same point estimates and human-rating information, without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match across the tables, figures and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains ALLD (2×) MSE 0.17 and BLEU 25.84, while Table 3 retains joint-training A/B accuracy 98.6% and BLEU 30.17.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Section 4.2, including Equations 1–2 and the accompanying reasoning, is unchanged. No definitions, assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about the descriptive speech-quality corpus, ALLD, numerical prediction performance and descriptive response quality.

C2.justification: Interpretations of encoder training, descriptive diversity, generalization and joint training are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same uncertainty about description–MOS mechanisms and limitations concerning word-level degradation explanations.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, generation prompts, SWD construction details and resource links are unchanged. The new correspondence line and revised support acknowledgment do not add implementation details or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the research positioning are identical. The acknowledgment replacement changes institutional credit, not the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds corresponding-author markers and contact information. It also replaces the Tencent/Tencent-NTU support acknowledgment with technical-support credit to NVIDIA Taiwan Research & Development Center. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added correspondence line slightly shifts the first-page layout, and Table 4 has small spacing and width adjustments. Figures, table contents, captions and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same methods, evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility information, including all appendix content. Correspondence details, revised institutional credit and small layout adjustments do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
